newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ACEVAL BECOMES LATEST GOALKEEPING MARKSMAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ACEVAL BECOMES LATEST GOALKEEPING MARKSMAN.

text.p: Danilo Aceval joined the South American legion of scoring goalkeepers on Wednesday when he struck twice for Paraguay's Cerro Porteno in the Libertadores Cup.
Aceval converted a penalty in each half as his team drew 2-2 with fellow Paraguayans Guarani in a first round, group one match.

Paraguay's Jose Luis Chilavert, who takes free-kicks as well as penalties for the national team and his Argentine club Velez Sarsfield, is the leading exponent, with Colombia's Rene Higuita not far behind.
But the idea of goalkeepers turning into strikers has recently become a fashion around Latin America.
Racing Club keeper Ignacio Gonzalez and Carlos Bossio of Estudiantes both made the scoresheet in the Argentine championship last year.

In Brazil, at least three goalkeepers have converted penalties this year, Rogerio of Sao Paulo has scored from a free-kick and Hiran of Guarani recently salvaged his team a 3-3 draw with Palmeiras by scoring with a last-minute header.
Aceval's marksmanship was not enough to lift his team off the bottom of group one. With two games to play they look doomed.
The battle in the first round of South America's top club competition is to avoid being the one team eliminated as the top three teams in each of the five groups progress to the next ground.
Racing Club of Argentina are in danger of being the unlucky team in group two after losing 1-0 to Chilavert's Velez, who are already mathematically qualified, on Wednesday.
Ecuador's Nacional also went through thanks to a 1-0 win over local rivals Emelec, who must now slug it out with Racing.

Mineros of Venezuela also face the axe after losing 1-0 to compatriots Minerven in group three where Colo Colo have already qualified and fellow Chileans Universidad Catolica look certain to progress.

Group four, which features Gremio and Cruzeiro of Brazil and Sporting Cristal and Alianza of Peru, is wide open after Cruzeiro, who lost their first three games, beat Gremio 1-0 away in a match marred by more than 50 fouls.

Palhinha scored the winning goal early in the second half while in Lima the two Peruvian sides drew 1-1. Any one of the teams could still miss out but Brazilians look safe and have home advantage in the remaining games.
